issues.legal_issue: A court exercising inherent jurisdiction should not quash criminal proceedings after investigation and filing of a charge sheet by evaluating disputed evidence or deciding serious triable allegations on their merits.
material_facts: The investigation included statements from the complainant, accused, and independent witnesses, collection of evidence from the scene, and culminated in a charge sheet; the Magistrate took cognizance.
The parties disputed whether a notarized document recording payment and transfer of possession was genuine and whether the stated payment had been made.
The High Court quashed the proceedings, treating the dispute as civil and assessing the allegations and materials without considering the investigation material.
issues.conclusion: The High Court exceeded its jurisdiction by quashing the proceedings on the merits of disputed, triable allegations. Its order was set aside and the criminal trial was to proceed in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 482 Cr.P.C., inherent power is exceptional and must be exercised sparingly, carefully, and with caution. At the FIR stage, the court considers whether the allegations disclose a cognizable offence; after investigation and filing of a charge sheet, it must also consider the material collected, but cannot appreciate disputed evidence, draw its own merits-based inferences, or act as an appellate court or conduct a trial. The Court relied on State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335; Dineshbhai Chandubhai Patel v. State of Gujarat, (2018) 3 SCC 104; Dhruvaram Murlidhar Sonar v. State of Maharashtra, (2019) 18 SCC 191; CBI v. Arvind Khanna, (2019) 10 SCC 686; Telangana v. Managipet, (2019) 19 SCC 87; and XYZ v. State of Gujarat, (2019) 10 SCC 337.

rule.if: appeal_against_criminal_quashing and investigation_material_collected and charge_sheet_filed and serious_disputed_triable_allegations and high_court_assessed_disputed_merits

predicates.appeal_against_criminal_quashing: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an order that quashed criminal proceedings.
predicates.investigation_material_collected: Investigators collected evidence and recorded statements during the investigation.
predicates.charge_sheet_filed: Investigators filed a charge sheet after completing the investigation.
predicates.serious_disputed_triable_allegations: The case includes serious allegations and material factual disputes that require determination at trial.
predicates.high_court_assessed_disputed_merits: The High Court evaluated disputed allegations or evidence on their merits while deciding whether to quash the proceedings.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges criminal quashing after a completed investigation and charge sheet, and serious disputed issues remain for trial, a merits-based assessment of those issues by the High Court results in the quashing order being set aside and the trial proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: Whether the alleged absence of entrustment defeats a criminal charge cannot be decided at the quashing stage when the alleged payment and transfer of possession are seriously disputed.
material_facts: The accused relied on a disputed notarized document said to record payment and transfer of possession.
The complainant disputed the payment, and one cheque given under the sale arrangement had been dishonoured.
The High Court found that no case of criminal breach of trust was made out, while treating the disputed document as a matter for civil proceedings.
issues.conclusion: It was premature to find that no case of criminal breach of trust was made out; the disputed matters were to be considered at trial.
issues.legal_principle: Applying Section 406 IPC, the Court held that, in light of the disputed payment and possession, the alleged circumstances could amount to entrustment and could not be conclusively assessed at the quashing stage. The Court relied on the principles governing Section 482 Cr.P.C. set out in State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335; Dineshbhai Chandubhai Patel v. State of Gujarat, (2018) 3 SCC 104; Dhruvaram Murlidhar Sonar v. State of Maharashtra, (2019) 18 SCC 191; CBI v. Arvind Khanna, (2019) 10 SCC 686; Telangana v. Managipet, (2019) 19 SCC 87; and XYZ v. State of Gujarat, (2019) 10 SCC 337, including the rule against deciding disputed evidence on its merits at that stage.

predicates.criminal_case_at_pretrial_quashing_stage: The matter concerns whether criminal proceedings should be quashed before trial.
predicates.alleged_property_possession_transfer: A party alleges that property or possession was transferred in the course of the underlying transaction.
predicates.alleged_payment_or_transfer_disputed: The parties seriously dispute whether the alleged payment or transfer occurred.

issues.definition: When criminal proceedings are challenged before trial and the alleged payment or transfer of possession is disputed, a finding that there was no entrustment is premature.

issues.legal_issue: Whether a complainant had authority to bring a complaint cannot be determined against the complainant at the quashing stage solely because the asserted authority document was not placed before the High Court.
material_facts: The complaint stated that its maker had been appointed as an attorney by the property owner.
The asserted power-of-attorney document was not placed on the record before the High Court.
The investigation included statements from the complainant, the accused, and independent witnesses.
issues.conclusion: Whether the complainant had the asserted authority was to be considered during trial, so the High Court erred in finding at the quashing stage that the complainant lacked locus.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that, where the complaint asserts authority and an investigation has followed, the question whether that authority existed is to be considered during trial rather than resolved at the quashing stage merely because the authority document was not filed with the High Court. This follows the limits on merits-based determinations under Section 482 Cr.P.C. described in State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335; Dineshbhai Chandubhai Patel v. State of Gujarat, (2018) 3 SCC 104; Dhruvaram Murlidhar Sonar v. State of Maharashtra, (2019) 18 SCC 191; CBI v. Arvind Khanna, (2019) 10 SCC 686; Telangana v. Managipet, (2019) 19 SCC 87; and XYZ v. State of Gujarat, (2019) 10 SCC 337.

predicates.criminal_case_at_pretrial_quashing_stage: The matter concerns whether criminal proceedings should be quashed before trial.
predicates.complaint_asserts_representative_authori: The complaint states that its maker was authorized to act for another person.
predicates.authority_document_not_filed_before_high: The document said to establish that authority was not placed before the High Court.
predicates.investigation_statements_recorded: The investigation included recording statements from relevant persons or witnesses.

issues.definition: When a complaint asserts representative authority, the authority document was not filed before the High Court, and investigation statements have been recorded, the authority question is deferred to trial rather than determined at the quashing stage.
